Position Overview The EUC Engineer is responsible for engineering, securing, automating, supporting, and continuously improving enterprise end-user computing platforms and services. The role focuses primarily on the management of Windows endpoints, Microsoft Intune, endpoint applications, operating-system lifecycle, security and compliance controls, device provisioning, endpoint monitoring, vulnerability remediation, and user-experience improvements. The EUC Engineer works across the full endpoint lifecycle—from engineering standards and solution design through testing, deployment, monitoring, remediation, production support, and retirement. The engineer is expected to move beyond individual break/fix activities by developing repeatable, scalable, secure, and automated solutions that improve endpoint reliability, employee experience, operational efficiency, security posture, and supportability. The role partners closely with Service Desk, Desktop Support, Security, Identity, Infrastructure, Cloud, Network, Application, Compliance, and business teams to ensure end-user technology services remain secure, stable, standardized, and aligned with organizational requirements. Role: EUC Engineer Key Responsibilities Manage and support Windows endpoints using Microsoft Intune and related Microsoft technologies. Develop and maintain device configuration profiles, compliance policies, security baselines, and endpoint standards. Support Windows 11 upgrades, device provisioning, imaging, Autopilot, and endpoint lifecycle activities. Package, test, deploy, update, and retire enterprise applications using Intune and other endpoint-management tools. Develop PowerShell scripts and automated remediation solutions to reduce manual effort and recurring support issues. Identify and remediate Critical and High-risk endpoint vulnerabilities and unsupported software. Implement and support endpoint security controls including BitLocker, Defender, device restrictions, Conditional Access, and compliance requirements. Support specialized and secure endpoint environments, including controlled or Cleanroom device configurations. Troubleshoot complex Windows, Intune, application, authentication, policy, and endpoint-related issues. Support integration between physical endpoints and Azure Virtual Desktop/WVD environments. Develop endpoint monitoring, reporting, dashboards, and analytics to identify health, compliance, and performance issues. Perform root-cause analysis and implement permanent engineering solutions for recurring incidents. Support Service Desk and Desktop Support teams through technical escalation, documentation, knowledge transfer, and engineering guidance. Participate in incident, problem, change, patch, and vulnerability-management processes. Maintain accurate technical documentation, implementation plans, operational procedures, and support runbooks. Continuously identify opportunities for endpoint standardization, automation, self-service, security improvement, and operational efficiency. Technical Skills Preferred experience with: Microsoft Intune Windows 10/11 Microsoft Entra ID / Azure AD Windows Autopilot PowerShell Microsoft Defender for Endpoint BitLocker Conditional Access Application packaging and deployment Intune Remediations Endpoint security and compliance Vulnerability and patch management Azure Log Analytics / Endpoint Analytics Azure Virtual Desktop / WVD Microsoft Graph API Git / GitHub or similar source-control tools Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or equivalent experience. Typically 3–6 years of experience in EUC, Endpoint Engineering, Desktop Engineering, Systems Engineering, or a related role. Hands-on experience with Microsoft Intune and enterprise Windows endpoint management. Strong troubleshooting, scripting, automation, and problem-solving skills. Ability to work effectively across Infrastructure, Security, Service Desk, Desktop Support, and business teams. Key Competencies Endpoint engineering and troubleshooting Automation and continuous improvement Security and compliance awareness Root-cause analysis Technical ownership Cross-functional collaboration Documentation and knowledge sharing Customer and employee experience focus Key Measures of Success Success in the role may be measured through: Endpoint compliance and security posture Reduction in vulnerabilities and unsupported software Application deployment success Windows upgrade and device lifecycle completion Reduction in recurring incidents Increased automation and automated remediation Improved endpoint reliability and user experience Reduction in manual support effort Successful delivery of EUC modernization initiatives Role Expectation The EUC Engineer is expected to move beyond individual device troubleshooting and focus on creating repeatable, secure, automated, and scalable endpoint solutions that improve reliability, security, supportability, and employee experience. title: Software Development Engineer, DSP Tech
description: DESCRIPTION Do you want to be part of the team that transforms how safety decisions are made for Amazon's Delivery Service Partners (DSPs) across 21 countries? Are you passionate about building intelligent, data driven platforms that protect delivery associates every single day? DSP SafetyTech is a newly formed team serving as the intelligence layer between safety signals and decisions — interpreting what happened, routing it to who can act, and ensuring no safety event goes unresolved. Today, safety data is fragmented across seven systems with no single technical owner, causing attribution errors, reconciliation gaps, and duplicated logic. We're changing that. We are looking for a Software Development Engineer to help build a governed safety intelligence platform. You will contribute to three critical pillars: Safety Data as a Service (SDaaS), a governed serving layer consolidating telematics, incidents, and contextual enrichment; DSP Facing Mechanisms, a unified configuration layer managing compound signals and business rules across DSP facing surfaces; and Advanced Analytics and Agentic Capabilities, predictive models and AI agents that provide actionable safety insights. This is a rare opportunity to join a team building a platform from the ground up that will directly impact the safety of delivery associates worldwide. Key job responsibilities Design, develop, test, and deploy software components for a governed data serving platform that consolidates telematics, incident reports, video evidence, and contextual enrichment from multiple upstream systems Build and maintain backend services and APIs that support a unified configuration layer where safety business rules are authored, validated, versioned, and distributed Develop frontend components for a consolidated safety dashboard, a single view where signals, scorecard outcomes, alerts, event video, and interventions come together • Implement compound safety signals that combine individual data sources into higher order, actionable safety indicators • Write clean, maintainable, and well tested code following software engineering best practices Participate in code reviews, design discussions, and operational excellence activities Collaborate with data engineers and data scientists to integrate data pipelines and model outputs into production services Contribute to automated evidence preservation mechanisms to address short video retention windows Troubleshoot and resolve production issues, participating in on call rotations to ensure system reliability Work with cross functional teams including product managers, stakeholders across investigations, claims, insurance, and accountability to understand requirements and deliver solutions A day in the life You will be part of a team building the safety intelligence backbone for Amazon's DSP ecosystem. Your day may involve writing and reviewing code for backend services, building frontend features for the safety dashboard, discussing design approaches with your team, or debugging a production issue. You will collaborate closely with data engineers and data scientists to bring data driven capabilities to life. You'll participate in sprint planning, stand ups, and retrospectives, contributing ideas to improve both the product and the development process. You will have the opportunity to learn and grow across the full stack, from data pipelines to user facing experiences, while working on a platform that scales across multiple countries. About the team DSP Safety Tech is a newly established team with a clear mission: convert every safety event into a clear, trusted action for every DSP, in every market, every time. Our North Star is ensuring every safety signal reaches the people who can act on it, with the context needed to make timely decisions, so risks are identified earlier, decisions are made consistently, and every Delivery Associate goes home safely. We operate at the intersection of data engineering, applied science, and product development, serving stakeholders from investigators to insurance to DSP owners themselves. We're building from the ground up with a strong vision, executive sponsorship, and the freedom to innovate across the full stack, from governed data pipelines to AI powered agentic experiences. BASIC QUALIFICATIONS 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience Experience programming with at least one software programming language PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. description: Experience: 3–6 Years Education: B.E. / B.Tech / B.Sc. in Computer Science, IT, or equivalent Work Location: On-site Industry: Defence Technology | Surveillance | AI | Real-Time Video Systems Job Description We are looking for an experienced Software Tester / QA Engineer to validate an integrated Surveillance & Command System involving real-time EO/IR video feeds, AI-based detection overlays, geospatial maps, alerts, and operator workflows. The ideal candidate will have strong experience in functional, regression, negative, exploratory, and performance/soak testing of complex web and backend applications. Experience with video streaming, AI/ML products, real-time systems, or multi-sensor platforms will be highly preferred. You will be responsible for identifying critical issues before deployment, validating end-to-end system behavior, and ensuring product reliability under realistic operational conditions. Key Responsibilities Execute release test plans across edge agents, central backend systems, and operator-facing web applications. Validate multi-feed EO/IR video, synchronization, AI overlays, confidence thresholds, object tracking, and playback/replay functionality. Perform functional, regression, exploratory, negative, and soak testing. Validate REST APIs and React-based operator interfaces, including live video, maps, alerts, reports, settings, and authentication. Test failure scenarios such as UDP packet loss, delayed camera connections, WebRTC reconnections, GPU overload, and AI engine failures. Maintain golden video clips and scenario-based test suites for validating model and sensor-fusion changes. Identify, document, and track defects with clear reproduction steps, expected vs. actual results, logs, screenshots, and video evidence. Perform regression testing after software, AI model, configuration, and engine updates. Coordinate with developers, system engineers, and operators during integration and acceptance testing. Prepare test reports and evidence packages to support certification and release readiness. description: Job Description: We are hiring a Senior SDET for Quality Assurance team. You will design and grow Playwright automation and the tooling around it, and you will use AI across the quality lifecycle: requirements analysis, test authoring, coverage review, debugging, and reporting. You will also own functional quality for your assigned applications. That includes manual and exploratory testing when human judgment is the better instrument. Automation and AI take the repeatable work so your manual effort goes where it adds the most value. You will work on applications that support ICE financial-markets infrastructure. A miss here is not cosmetic: defects can affect trading, clearing, data integrity, or regulatory evidence. We need someone who tests with that risk in mind. This is a hands-on Senior individual contributor role. You will influence design through code, reviews, and pairing. You will not manage people, and you will not be the sole owner of the organization-wide framework. Responsibilities Test automation Design, build, and maintain Playwright automation across UI, API, and integration layers. Evolve the shared framework: page and component abstractions, fixtures, test data, environment configuration, CI/CD integration, and reporting. Apply automation standards and design patterns that keep suites fast, reliable, and readable. Reduce flakiness and improve execution speed through metrics and root-cause analysis. Run automated suites in CI/CD and partner with DevOps on environments and pipeline reliability. AI-enabled quality workflow Use AI coding agents in your daily workflow to accelerate automation authoring, refactoring, debugging, and maintenance. Use AI tooling to review requirements for ambiguities, missing edge cases, and untestable criteria before development begins. Generate test cases from requirements, then refine, consolidate, and prioritize them with engineering judgment. You own the final suite, not the model. Find coverage gaps, duplicate effort, and weak assertions in existing suites. Adopt and extend AI tooling where it pays off. Building custom agent skills or MCP servers is a plus, not the core of the job. Functional test ownership Own functional coverage and test strategy for assigned applications across UI, services, and integration points. Decide what to automate and what to keep manual based on risk, stability, execution frequency, and maintenance cost. Expect a mix of automation and exploratory work, weighted toward automation once a flow is stable. Perform manual, exploratory, and scenario-based testing where human judgment matters most. Triage, reproduce, and document defects, and drive them to resolution. Provide evidence-based release readiness to engineering and product leadership. Produce clear reporting on coverage, execution results, defect trends, and release risk. Technical influence Raise the quality of automation through code review and pairing with QA engineers. Share practical patterns for automation, AI-assisted testing, and when manual testing is still the better approach. Partner with software engineers, product managers, and DevOps to move quality work earlier in the delivery cycle. What you will work with Playwright, TypeScript or JavaScript, Node, Git, and CI/CD pipelines. AI coding agents used as part of normal engineering work. Jira and Xray (or equivalent) for defects, plans, and execution evidence. API testing against REST and, where present, GraphQL. Knowledge and Experience 7+ years in software quality engineering or SDET roles, including 5+ years of hands-on test automation. Hands-on experience with Playwright or a comparable modern E2E framework (Cypress, WebdriverIO, or similar), including suite structure, test data, and CI execution—not only recording or copying tests. Strong TypeScript or JavaScript and sound software engineering fundamentals: modular design, version control, code review, and refactoring. Applied experience using AI-assisted engineering tools in a routine workflow (coding agents, AI-assisted test authoring, or AI-supported requirements and code analysis). API test automation experience across REST or GraphQL. Experience contributing to a test automation framework and integrating automated tests into CI/CD. Strong functional testing foundation: test design techniques, risk-based prioritization, boundary and negative testing, and structured exploratory testing. Working knowledge of Jira, Xray, or equivalent defect and test management tools. Clear written and verbal communication. Test plans, defect reports, and quality summaries should be usable asynchronously. Ability to work on-site in Atlanta five days per week. Preferred Qualifications Deep Playwright experience: framework architecture, flakiness mitigation, test data strategy, and execution at scale in CI. Hands-on experience with AI coding agents and AI tools. Experience creating AI agent skills, custom agents, or Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. Contract testing experience. Experience helping a QA team adopt automation and AI practices in a practical, sustainable way. Background in a regulated or high-reliability domain, ideally financial markets, trading, clearing, or market data.

title: Builder QA II
description: Job Description You are an engineer who specialises in proving things work. The distinction between “dev” and “QA” work is not one we maintain: you read the application code, you write production-grade Python, and you build agents. The difference is what you point them at. 1. Core DNA AI-Native Workflow. You use AI to accelerate everything you do as a default, not an experiment. You have opinions about which tools earn their place. Agentic Implementation. You build, debug and deploy autonomous agents — LLM-driven test generation, Playwright browser-use agents, self-healing locator strategies — against complex ERP screens and workflows. Legacy-to-Modern Bridge. Some of what you’ll test is a modern web rewrite. Some is a desktop application older than your career. Both are puzzles. Evidence Over Confidence. A generated test that has never been executed is not a test. You know your own false-positive and flake rates rather than claiming there aren’t any. 2. What You Own The ticket-to-test pipeline. An agent that reads a requirement or defect, understands the affected area, and produces a real test — grounded in the actual application, not in what the model imagines the application looks like. Hallucinated locators are the failure mode that kills these systems; preventing them is your problem. Execution and stabilization. Generation is the easy half. Your pipeline isn’t done when a test file exists or a ticket gets created — it’s done when the test has run against a real build, passed repeatedly, and earned its place in the suite. Flake is the enemy, because a suite nobody trusts is worse than no suite. Coverage that means something. You can tell the difference between a suite that covers the code and a suite that covers the risk. You use mutation testing and real defect history rather than counting tests, and you argue for the edge cases that actually bite: fiscal calendars, multi-currency, partial shipments, period-end adjustments. 3. Where You Might Lean In Test Generation & Grounding — the retrieval and context problem. How does an agent know what the screen really contains, what the business rule really is, and what changed in this release? Adversarial & Red-Team — you build agents whose job is to break things. Programmatic prompt optimization (DSPy), fuzzing business logic, hunting the input nobody thought of. Test Infrastructure & Agent-Ops — the factory the test agents run in: parallel execution, environment and data management, tracing, and the observability to know why a run went sideways. Legacy Surface Automation — desktop and thick-client applications where modern tooling doesn’t reach and the automation has to be built rather than installed. What You’ll Actually Do Build test-generation agents that take a ticket and produce an executable test grounded in the live application. Close the loop. Make generation, execution, stabilization and reporting one pipeline rather than four disconnected steps with a human carrying work between them. Automate the untestable. Wrap legacy business logic — the modules everyone has avoided because there’s no spec — in characterization tests that capture what the system actually does today. Kill flake. Find the root cause rather than adding a retry. Retries are how suites die. Red-team the financial logic. Build the agents that go looking for the case where the ledger doesn’t balance. Fix your own agents in production. Read the traces, find why it went sideways, make it not happen again. What Good Looks Like (Illustrative — real targets agreed with the hiring manager.) 30 days: Shipped your first agent-generated test into a running suite — generated, executed, stable. 90 days: Owning the ticket-to-test pipeline for a product area end to end, with a measured flake rate and a real coverage picture. 6 months: Other Builders reuse what you built. Escaped defects in your area are measurably down, and you can show why. The Stack Python, pytest, Playwright, SQL (Postgres/SQL Server), TypeScript, OpenAI/Anthropic, LangChain/LangGraph, DSPy, pgvector/Qdrant, Docker, CI/CD pipelines, OpenTelemetry, eval and tracing platforms (LangSmith / Langfuse / Braintrust or equivalent), desktop automation frameworks where the application demands it. And any other tool that helps us achieve greatness. Who You Are You’ve shipped one. You have built at least one autonomous agent or complex LLM workflow that real people used for real work — not a weekend demo. You know how it failed, because it did. You write real code. Python that goes to production and gets reviewed like anyone else’s. If your automation experience stops at a record-and-playback tool, this isn’t the role. The manual-task hater. You have a physical reaction to repetitive work. If you do it twice, you’ve already started drafting the automation. Technically fearless. A 500-table undocumented legacy schema isn’t complexity, it’s a puzzle about to get solved. You aren’t intimidated by spaghetti code — you’re the one who brings the sauce. Rigor over hype. You love the new models and you still ask for the numbers. You know the difference between a cool demo and a pipeline people rely on every release. Suspicious by instinct. Your first question about any green build is what it didn’t check. Why Join Us Quality is engineering here, not a stage gate. You are a Builder on the same ladder, with the same levels and the same expectations as everyone else in the squad. You build; you don’t sign off on other people’s work. The Final Boss of complexity. ERPs are the ultimate challenge for AI. If you can build agents that validate a General Ledger, you’ve solved the hardest version of this problem. Agentic autonomy. We don’t do tickets. We do missions. You’ll have real freedom over the models, frameworks and agent architectures you think will win. No red tape. If the agent works and the evals pass, we ship. No Change Management Committee — a “Does It Work?” policy. The Builder Tribe. You won’t be the only AI person in the room. You’ll be part of a small squad equally obsessed with moving faster, where your automation hacks are your biggest contribution rather than a hidden side project.
